sections.h2: What should a seller know about Greene County, Tennessee?
sections.html:
Greene County fills a wide stretch of Tennessee's eastern border, with Greeneville serving as the seat and the biggest town. Its 624 square miles are almost entirely land. Settlers organized it in 1783 from Washington County, North Carolina, and gave it the name of Revolutionary War general Nathanael Greene. Davy Crockett was born here in 1786, and Tusculum is home to what Wikipedia calls the oldest college in Tennessee.

Long ridges and narrow valleys make up most of the terrain. Bays Mountain marks much of the line with Hawkins County on the north, and the far southeast corner rises into the Bald Mountains along the North Carolina border. The Nolichucky River runs through the southern half and backs up behind Nolichucky Dam into Davy Crockett Lake. Interstate 81, US 11E and US 321 are the main highways.

Tusculum is the county's one city, and Baileyton, Greeneville and Mosheim are towns. Greeneville City Schools covers addresses inside the Greeneville limits, while Greene County Schools serves everything outside them. Buyers ask about that line early, so know which district your street falls in.

Census QuickFacts gives this snapshot of the county:

  • Population of 73,831 in mid-2025, which is 5.2 percent above the April 2020 count
  • 33,581 housing units, and 77.1 percent of households own their home
  • Typical owner-occupied value of $207,500 across 2020 to 2024, with monthly owner costs of $1,150 for those with a mortgage and $361 for those without
  • Household income of $56,194 and 16.3 percent of residents under the poverty line
  • 276 new building permits during 2025

sections.h2: Which Greene County offices handle property tax?
sections.html:
Three local bodies split the work. An elected assessor decides what each parcel is worth, the county commission chooses the rate, and the elected trustee mails the bill and banks the payment. The trustee's page says plainly that the trustee has no say in how large a bill is.

Trustee Nathan Holt works out of the Greene County Government Administration Center, 401 Takoma Avenue, Suite 104, Greeneville, TN 37743, on 423-798-1705. Hours run Monday to Friday, 8 a.m. until 5 p.m. The county technical assistance service lists Assessor of Property Chuck Jeffers at 401 Takoma Avenue, Suite 106, on 423-798-1738.

The Town of Greeneville taxes property too. Its Recorder's Office accepts those payments, so a home inside town limits generates a county bill and a town bill. For addresses in Mosheim, Baileyton or Tusculum, ask who collects the municipal share. The Comptroller says a city's collecting official may be its treasurer, its recorder or the county trustee.

sections.h2: How is a Greene County property tax bill figured?
sections.html:
The Trustee gives the formula as assessed value times the rate, divided by $100. Tennessee sets the assessed value at 25 percent of appraised value for homes and farms and 40 percent for commercial and industrial property.

The Trustee's own example takes a $25,000 assessed value and a $1.8731 rate, producing $468.28 that rounds to $468. It is labeled as a sample only. Put a house at the county's typical $207,500 and the assessed figure lands at $51,875. Multiply by the current rate and divide by 100 to get the county share. Ask the Trustee for the rate in force, since the commission and the town set theirs on their own schedules.

The Trustee also explains where the revenue goes. Property tax is the biggest local source for the general fund, with the wheel tax second. The school fund leans mostly on state education dollars, followed by property tax and local sales tax.

sections.h2: When is Greene County property tax due and how can I pay it?
sections.html:
Collection for the 2026 county bills began on Monday, October 5, 2026 and continues interest-free into late winter. Bills turn delinquent on March 1. As of November 15, 2026, the bill is open and not yet late.

The county mails a notice, though state law does not make it do so. A missing notice is no defense against interest. Call 423-798-1705 if yours never came, and call the Assessor on 423-798-1738 to correct your address on file.

The Trustee accepts payment these ways:

  • Over the counter at Suite 104 using cash, check, money order or a debit or credit card
  • By mail, with the stub enclosed and the receipt number noted on the check, and a postmark is accepted
  • By phone at 1-833-591-7184 or online at tnproptax.com
  • Through the deposit slot just inside the Administration Center's main entrance

A vendor charges 2.5 percent on cards and $1.25 on online ACH payments. The county keeps none of it.

sections.h2: What is the path for contesting a Greene County property value?
sections.html:
Your first stop is the county's equalization board, which starts hearing cases on June 1 each year. Skip it and the value generally stands. The Assessor's office is where you ask to be scheduled.

An owner who loses there can carry the case to the State Board of Equalization. The filing window closes August 1 of that tax year, or 45 days after the county board mailed its decision if that comes later. A state judge holds a hearing and rules in writing within 90 days. You carry the burden of showing the right number, and you can reach the state board at 615-401-7883.

The state's advice on persuasive proof:

  • Closed sales of similar houses, with allowances for size, age, condition and location
  • An appraiser's report, with the appraiser ready to appear
  • A concrete dollar value you propose, since simply calling the house overvalued rarely works

Meanwhile, pay the undisputed share of the bill by the delinquency date and settle any prior-year balances, or the case may be stalled or thrown out.

sections.h2: Which tax breaks can Greene County homeowners use?
sections.html:
Tennessee runs a refund-style relief program for low-income seniors, disabled owners, disabled veterans and certain surviving spouses. In 2026 an elderly or disabled applicant's 2025 income cannot exceed $38,470, and the refund is worked out on no more than $33,600 of market value. For veterans the cap on value is $175,000. Applicants must own and occupy the home, and seniors must turn 65 by December 31, 2026.

Because it reimburses taxes already paid, you still settle the bill first. Greene County's Trustee takes applications from the first Monday of October through March and wants a phone call beforehand to list the documents. The state brochure ties the final date to 35 days past delinquency, so confirm the exact day with the office.

A separate local-option freeze exists for owners 65 and up. The Comptroller's list of 28 adopting counties does not include Greene, so ask the Trustee if that changed.

sections.h2: What happens to the bill when a Greene County house sells?
sections.html:
According to the Trustee, the buyer and seller normally divide the year's tax at the closing table, and the Trustee's staff takes no part in that split. The title company or closing agent does the math and shows it on the settlement statement.

If you owe back tax, get a payoff figure from the Trustee early because interest keeps building. Sellers dealing with an inherited home, a vacant property or a long repair list can ask the title company to pay the balance out of proceeds. Recording the deed and the $0.37 per $100 state transfer tax happen at the register of deeds when the deed is recorded.

faqs.q: What is the Greene County property tax rate?
faqs.a: Call the Trustee at 423-798-1705 for the current figure, since the county commission and the Town of Greeneville each set a rate. The formula is assessed value times the rate divided by 100, with homes assessed at 25 percent of appraised value.

faqs.q: When do Greene County property taxes go delinquent?
faqs.a: March 1. Payments for 2026 were accepted starting October 5, 2026 and carry no interest through the end of February. After that, interest is charged until the balance is cleared.

faqs.q: Who should I contact about my Greene County property value?
faqs.a: The Assessor of Property at 423-798-1738, at 401 Takoma Avenue, Suite 106 in Greeneville. That office answers value questions, updates mailing addresses and starts the process toward the county equalization board.

faqs.q: Can seniors in Greene County get a tax break?
faqs.a: Yes, through the state relief program if 2025 income was $38,470 or less and the applicant owns and lives in the home. The Trustee takes applications. The local freeze exists only where a county adopted it, and Greene is not on the state's list.

faqs.q: Who pays the property tax at a Greene County closing?
faqs.a: Both sides, by proration. The Trustee says taxes are typically prorated at closing and that its own office does not split them. Your title company or closing agent does it.
